purpose: Replace the rejected regular square-block material and procedural ivy

prompts.concept: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: visual target for rebuilding an actual game material. Edit the supplied rejected game screenshot. Replace ONLY the flat repeated square-block wall with believable aged European hill-town fortification masonry: subtly warm grey limestone, irregular coursed rubble and squared stone mixed, varied stone lengths from 25 to 75 cm, variable 15 to 35 cm course heights, occasional small infill stones. Narrow, pale lime mortar sits behind softly worn chipped stone edges. The broad faces of the stones should be relatively calm and solid, with fine natural pits, not uniformly corrugated or crusty. Gentle mineral stains and restrained damp at the foot, no dramatic high-contrast grunge. Aim for photographic quality in a grounded modern first-person game, understated and convincing. Keep the same wall plane, camera, crop, lighting direction, ground geometry and ivy silhouette/placement; do not add new objects. Avoid repeated checkerboard blocks, perfectly straight industrial brick rows, dark outlined cartoon joints, heavy brown contrast, excessive bump noise, and glossy stone. Keep the reference spatially feasible to reproduce as a material; no new wall geometry or large protrusions.
prompts.color: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless PBR BASE COLOR texture for an actual 3D game stone wall, not a scene. Use the supplied reference ONLY for its limestone masonry character. Create a flat, orthographic, unlit/de-lit texture covering a 4 by 4 metre patch of aged European limestone fortification. Full image is uninterrupted masonry from edge to edge. Natural irregular coursed stone, elongated and chunky stones of varied sizes, softly chipped edges, thin pale-grey lime mortar with occasional small infill. Course heights vary about 15â€“35 cm, stone lengths 25â€“75 cm; do not produce a square-block grid. Stones are restrained warm grey, taupe and muted grey-beige with subtle mineral variation. Surface detail is photographic and fine, broad faces relatively quiet, worn rather than heavily corrugated. Keep albedo contrast moderate; mortar slightly darker than stone but not black. Seamless periodic tile: left edge must join right and top edge must join bottom, including complete stone and mortar shapes. Neutral diffuse calibration, no directional lighting, no highlights, no cast shadows, no AO baked into the color, no gradient/vignette, no greenery, no moss, no ground, no sky, no text, no border. Prefer a high-resolution square output, at least 2048px square if possible. The result will be tiled over a large wall so avoid any conspicuous unique stain, crack or isolated bright stone.
prompts.height: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: exact matching grayscale HEIGHT DATA MAP for this PBR masonry color texture. Convert the input texture into a height map; preserve every stone outline, mortar path, small infill, chip and edge position EXACTLY, pixel aligned and in the identical square crop. Do not invent or shift stones. The recessed mortar bed is dark grey (value about 45/255). Each stone's broad face is smooth mid-light grey (about 185/255), with tiny controlled height variation regardless of how dark its original COLOR was; dark colored stones must still be high. Gently soften/chip the stone rim into the mortar across a few pixels (values 80 to 170). Fine pits on the face have very low amplitude, at most 10 grey levels, not a noisy interpretation of every color fleck. Remove lighting, shadows, stains, white calcite spots and pigmentation completely; represent only physical depth. Height is high stone faces and low mortar, not a grayscale photo. Keep matched seamless edge structure. Pure neutral grayscale only, no color tint, no text, no border. This must register precisely with the source color texture as material data.
prompts.ivy: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: high-resolution RGBA climbing ivy cutout for a 3D wall foliage card. The input is a silhouette guide, NOT the desired white color. Replace the white shape with photorealistic English ivy, and replace all black with genuine transparency. Preserve the overall tall 1:2 footprint: a dense irregular rooted mass touching the bottom edge, narrower climbing stems rising to sparse tendrils, a high central-left tip and lower right tip, numerous small gaps between individual leaves. Each small leaf has the actual three-to-five pointed lobes, delicate veins, slight cupping and organically turned orientations. Rich restrained forest/olive greens with a few lighter new leaves, natural brown thin branches. Diffuse soft daylight, believable leaf overlap depth and fine detail, no dark wall or soil baked into the background. Preserve comfortable transparent margin at the sides and top; do not crop off leaves except roots at the bottom. Avoid cartoon or geometric leaves, star outlines, giant foreground leaves, black halos and smooth painted blobs. Transparent background, no checkerboard pixels, no text. Produce a portrait 1:2 aspect ratio texture with detailed individual leaves appropriate to a roughly 1 metre wide, 2 metre tall plant patch.

uv_data_method: Tools/belltower_wall_quilt.py: numerical UV selectors and per-stone luminance; original ImageGen color/height pixels retained
